models.name: food production and calorie correction
models.summary: Regional food is plantation plus husbandry plus fishery. Plantation is yield times area. Husbandry adds unit meat, unit milk, and unit egg, then multiplies by headcount. Fishery is unit catch times area. The calorie block multiplies each of those terms by a rice-based ratio and by the rice benchmark.
models.purpose: turn three food sources into a mass and then into a calorie total
objectives: quantify production and the calories in that production
constraints: only food crops, and only meat, eggs, and milk, are counted
assumptions: Wikipedia's three sources stand for a national food system
rice per 100 grams is the benchmark 1

models.name: transporter profit and selection
models.summary: Acquisition cost is production times a share times a unit price. Sales revenue is volume times sale price. One trip's profit subtracts the origin acquisition cost and a freight term from the destination sales revenue. A greedy loop then sends each food toward the living area with the largest profit.
models.purpose: choose a destination for each food by the transporter's profit
constraints: one living area is one transporter
freight inside a living area is zero
assumptions: a transporter moves one food at a time

models.name: indicators and weighted objective
models.summary: Entropy weights combine emissions, cultivated land, and water into a sustainability score. Equity is the hunger ratio. Profit is revenue minus production cost. The objective minimizes a gamma-weighted sum of the two scores divided by their five-year means, and one weight vector is printed for France and India.
models.purpose: score the food system and minimize a mix of the hunger ratio and the sustainability score
objectives: minimize the weighted objective with profit kept at or above zero
constraints: profit during the optimization is not less than zero
gamma runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1
assumptions: a larger equity score is a larger hunger share, and the objective minimizes it
